children: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), which holds a 10.72 per cent stake in the National Stock Exchange (NSE), may consider increasing its holding after the exchange's proposed initial public offering (IPO), Managing Director and CEO R Doraiswamy told The Hindu BusinessLine in an exclusive interview.

LIC has decided not to sell its NSE shares through the proposed offer-for-sale (OFS), signalling its confidence in the long-term value of the exchange. "We have taken a call not to be a seller. We will look at the process, look at the price and then take a call whether to enhance our stake or not," Doraiswamy said, as quoted by The Hindu BusinessLine.

The LIC chief said the insurer could emerge as a buyer depending on the valuation and market conditions. "We invest in stocks that, in our assessment, have the potential to create long-term value. Our size also means we can act as a financial institution and market stabiliser," he said.

The insurer's operational focus, however, remains on expanding life insurance penetration across India. LIC aims to establish a presence in every village panchayat, building on its existing coverage of around 92 per cent of districts and nearly 56 per cent of panchayats, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

One of the objectives for which the corporation was formed is to spread the message of life insurance to every nook and corner of the country," Doraiswamy said. "We are identifying panchayats where there is no LIC agent available and ensuring representation there." LIC expects to make substantial progress towards full panchayat coverage over the next one to two years.

The rural expansion is being supported by LIC's agency network, including its Bima Sakhi initiative. The insurer has around 2.8 lakh active women agents under the programme, helping strengthen last-mile insurance distribution.

LIC is also seeking to combine its established trust with a more technology-driven operating model as customer expectations evolve. "We need to stay relevant to the current generation by providing solutions that are available at their fingertips," Doraiswamy said, as quoted by The Hindu BusinessLine.

On the product side, LIC is continuing its shift towards higher-margin non-participating products. Their share has increased from around 7-8 per cent of annualised premium equivalent (APE) at the time of LIC's listing to nearly 30 per cent currently. "We would like to keep it around 30-35 per cent," Doraiswamy said.

At the group level, LIC is reviewing the performance of its subsidiaries, associate companies and overseas operations, with an emphasis on their contribution to profitability. "We are a financial conglomerate, and we expect every one of them to contribute to the overall profitability," he said.

title: LIC may raise NSE stake after IPO, won't sell in OFS, says CEO R Doraiswamy
